titre.sous: If + present, will. If + past, would.

aparte.texte: But I do not have more time.

piege.titre: Never will or would after if

q.lu: If the client ------- the offer, we **will sign** on Friday.

etapes.texte: Find the verb in the **other half** of the sentence
**will** goes with if + present, **would** with if + past

phrases.texte: Conditionals: types one and two.
A conditional sentence has two halves: the condition with if, and the result.
Type one is a real possibility: if plus present, then will.
Type two is an imaginary situation: if plus past, then would.
Type one. If the train is late, we will take a taxi.
It can really happen today. So we use the present after if, and will in the result.
Type two. If I had more time, I would learn Spanish.
But I do not have more time. It is only an idea. So we use the past after if, and would in the result.
Now, the big trap. We never put will or would just after if.
phrases.dit: Now, the big trap. We never put will, or would, just after if.

phrases.texte: If the train will be late is wrong. We say: if the train is late.
phrases.dit: If the train will be late, is wrong. We say: if the train is late.

phrases.texte: Now, a TOEIC question from Part 5. If the client, blank, the offer, we will sign on Friday.
phrases.dit: Now, a TOEIC question from Part five. If the client, blank, the offer, we will sign on Friday.

phrases.texte: A: accepts. B: will accept. C: accepted. D: accepting.
phrases.dit: Answer A. accepts. Answer B. will accept. Answer C. accepted. Answer D. accepting.

phrases.texte: Which answer is correct?
Look at the other half of the sentence: we will sign. Will tells you it is type one.
phrases.dit: Look at the other half of the sentence: we will sign. Will, tells you it is type one.

phrases.texte: B is wrong: no will after if. C is wrong: the past goes with would.
D is not a full verb. So A is correct: if the client accepts the offer, we will sign on Friday.
Remember three steps. One: find the verb in the other half of the sentence.
Two: will goes with if plus present. Would goes with if plus past.
Three: never will or would just after if.
